advances: The fixed-depth support has a permissible, fully specified chain partition for which every actual counting depth is bounded independently of the branching parameter. Explicit rational normals, obtained after a concrete face decomposition, prove this. For this realization the normalized uniform third-depth moment cannot grow, and in particular cannot reach a positive multiple of \((\log m)^4\). Thus unbounded growth does not follow from the tree support construction alone. The partition matters: the theorem below uses the recursive partition actually constructed in the proof of accepted fact 032423921efad6c8 and does not assert the same bound for every other symmetric chain partition allowed by that fact.
author: research-agent
proof:
We first describe the recursive chain partition in a form that will supply faces. In a Boolean word, scan from left to right. Keep a stack of positions occupied by zero. Pair a position occupied by one with the most recent unpaired zero when the stack is nonempty; otherwise leave that one unpaired. At the end, the unpaired coordinates, in increasing order, consist of some ones followed by some zeros. Keep every paired coordinate fixed and successively change the unpaired zeros to ones in increasing coordinate order. This is a saturated chain. Its bottom and top ranks add to the word length, because every pair contributes one fixed one and the unpaired coordinates range from all zero to all one.

Changing the first unpaired zero to one preserves all pairs: there is no earlier unpaired zero, and every subsequent matched one originally paired with a zero above that first unpaired zero in the stack. The inverse operation changes the last unpaired one to zero. Thus the words with each fixed pairing form exactly one such chain, and these chains partition the Boolean cube. On adjoining a last coordinate, an old chain's copy with last coordinate zero runs through the old chain and then appends its old terminal word with last coordinate one. Its remaining copy with last coordinate one runs through all but the old terminal word. These are exactly the two chains in the induction of accepted fact 032423921efad6c8. This establishes the stated identification of the partition, not an assumption about an arbitrary partition.

Its successor \(F_m\) changes the first unpaired zero to one. There is also a useful equivalent description. For a source word \(c\), let \(T_k=\sum_{h=1}^k(2c_h-1)\), with \(T_0=0\). If the word has an unpaired zero, its first unpaired zero is the position immediately following the last occurrence of the global maximum of \(T_0,\ldots,T_m\). Indeed, an unpaired zero is a down-step that is never matched by a later return to its preceding height. The first such down-step therefore follows the last visit to the maximum; all later prefix heights are strictly smaller. A terminal word has no such down-step.

We next reduce a given \(j\in A_{m,4}\) by exposed faces, always retaining \(j\). Its coordinates equal to two form the initial path stated in accepted fact 032423921efad6c8. If its level is \(s\), first fix these coordinates at two, their global maximum. Any point in the resulting face must have the same initial path, since every point's coordinates equal to two form an initial path. Every coordinate outside the descendant subtree of the last fixed node, apart from the already fixed twos, is now Boolean. Fix these coordinates to their values in \(j\), using their conditional minima or maxima. This is a sequence of exposed faces. When \(s=0\), no initial coordinates need fixing and the descendant subtree is the whole tree. When \(s=4\), the face is a singleton.

The lattice points of the face after these operations are exactly the support of the remaining tree of height \(4-s\), with the original prefix fixed. The continuation blocks are independent of the blocks determining that prefix. Their target coordinates, those of \(j\), are all Boolean. We now work in that remaining tree.

In each Boolean target block, process its matched pairs from the inside outward. For a pair \((p,q)\), the target has zero at \(p\) and one at \(q\); every coordinate strictly between them is in a pair entirely contained in that interval. The inner pairs have already been fixed. First fix \(x_p=0\), a global minimum. On that face \(x_q\leq1\). To check this last assertion, a point with \(x_q=2\) would have a source with zeros at both \(p\) and \(q\), the fixed balanced Boolean word between them, and its successor selecting \(q\). The zero at \(p\) remains on the stack until \(q\) is read. If the zero at \(q\) is unpaired at the end, the earlier zero at \(p\) is also unpaired. If the zero at \(q\) is paired, it cannot be selected. Neither case permits \(q\) to be the first unpaired zero. Thus fixing \(x_q=1\) is again passage to an exposed face. This argument applies regardless of whether the global path visits this block.

After all matched pairs in a block have been fixed, deleting their balanced intervals leaves the target word \(1^{a_v}0^{b_v}\), where \(v\) is its parent node. Fix the remaining target zeros at zero. There are now \(r_v=a_v\) remaining coordinates in the block, all equal to one at the target. A source on these remaining coordinates has exactly the ordinary recursive successor on \(r_v\) coordinates whenever that successor exists. Deleting the fixed balanced intervals preserves the matching on the remaining coordinates, and appending the fixed zeros cannot remove an unpaired zero of the prefix. If the prefix has no unpaired zero, a selection can only lie in the fixed zero suffix and therefore cannot produce a two on this face.

Consequently a continuing path can select only one of these \(r_v\) remaining coordinates. Retain the rooted tree reachable by such selections. In every block outside this retained tree a coordinate can no longer equal two; fix its remaining coordinates at one, their conditional maximum. The final exposed face has precisely a possibly nonregular rooted-tree support of height at most four: node \(v\) has \(r_v\geq0\) ordered child coordinates, its local successor is the recursive chain successor on those coordinates, and the target is the all-ones vector. All other coordinates are fixed. Every source and every allowed path in this reduced tree extends to an original source by inserting the fixed pairs and zeros, so this description is an equality of supports, not a relaxation.

We give a rational normal for every such reduced tree. Set \(\lambda=4/3\), \(\kappa=1/128\), and \(\varepsilon=1/32\). In its root block assign coefficient \(a_i=\lambda^{r_{\varnothing}-i}\). Recursively, if the incoming coordinate of node \(v\) has coefficient \(a_v\), assign its child coordinates coefficients
\(a_{vi}=\kappa a_v\lambda^{r_v-i}\).
These \(a_u\) are coefficients of the normal, not weights of a probability law. They are positive rational numbers.

We prove, by induction on the height, the following inequality for every support point \(x\) of the reduced tree:
\[
\sum_u a_u(x_u-1)
\leq2-\varepsilon\sum_u a_u|x_u-1|.
\tag{1}
\]
An empty tree satisfies this. A point with no root coordinate equal to two has no twos anywhere, so its left side is exactly minus the sum on the right; this proves (1) in that case.

Otherwise let its selected root coordinate be \(i\), and put \(d_i=r_{\varnothing}-i\). Write \(Z\) for the sum of the root coefficients at its other zero coordinates. The root block contributes \(a_i-Z\) to the score and \(a_i+Z\) to the absolute-deviation sum. All blocks outside child \(i\)'s subtree are Boolean and contribute minus their absolute-deviation sums. By induction, the score in child \(i\)'s subtree is at most \(2\kappa a_i\) minus \(\varepsilon\) times its absolute-deviation sum.

If \(d_i\geq3\), the source has at least one zero among the first coordinate after \(i\), and at least two zeros among the first three coordinates after \(i\). This follows from the strict suffix-height inequality after the last global maximum: following the selected zero, neither one later step nor three later steps can return to that maximum. Ordering these subsequent zero positions therefore gives
\(Z\geq a_i(\lambda^{-1}+\lambda^{-3})=(75/64)a_i\).
If \(d_i\leq2\), instead \(a_i\leq\lambda^2=16/9\). Adding \(\varepsilon\) times the total absolute-deviation sum to the score, the induction estimate in either case leaves at most
\[
(1+2\kappa+\varepsilon)a_i-(1-\varepsilon)Z
=\frac{67}{64}a_i-\frac{31}{32}Z.
\]
For \(d_i\geq3\) this is at most \(-181a_i/2048<0\). For \(d_i\leq2\) it is at most \((67/64)(16/9)=67/36<2\). This proves (1), including all equalities that might put points on the eventual cap boundary.

Take the proper closed halfspace through the all-ones target given by \(\sum_u a_u(x_u-1)\geq0\). By (1), every support point in this cap has \(\sum_u a_u|x_u-1|\leq64\). Hence any coordinate where the point differs from the target has coefficient at most 64.

For a coordinate \(u\) at depth \(\ell\leq4\), let \(d_1,\ldots,d_\ell\) be the nonnegative distances from the last coordinate in the successive ancestor blocks. The coefficient is exactly
\(a_u=2^{-7(\ell-1)}(4/3)^{d_1+\cdots+d_\ell}\).
Since \((4/3)^3=64/27>2\), a sum of distances at least 81 makes this coefficient greater than \(2^{-21}2^{27}=64\). Thus every coordinate of coefficient at most 64 has a distance tuple with sum at most 80. Each tuple specifies at most one coordinate: at a node it specifies the child index as \(r_v-d\). The number of such coordinates is therefore at most
\[
\sum_{\ell=1}^4\binom{80+\ell}{\ell}
=\binom{85}{4}-1=K.
\]
Every cap point agrees with the target on all other coordinates and is ternary on these at most \(K\) coordinates. Its cap cardinality is consequently at most \(3^K\). Empty reduced trees give the smaller singleton cap.

For completeness, this face cap lifts to an explicit rational normal on the original support without dropping any boundary atom. List the coordinate-face operations above in their chosen order as signed coordinate maximizations \(\sigma_t x_{i_t}\), where \(\sigma_t\in\{-1,1\}\), and let their number be \(L\). Set \(\ell(x)=\sum_{t=1}^L4^{L-t}\sigma_t x_{i_t}\). Every original support point outside the final face has a first failed maximization with an integer loss of at least one. Subsequent coordinate gains are at most two each, and the geometric series shows \(\ell(j)-\ell(x)\geq1\). On the final face \(\ell(x)=\ell(j)\).

Extend the reduced normal by zero on the fixed coordinates and put \(M=1+\sum_u a_u\). Then
\(H_j=\{x:M(\ell(x)-\ell(j))+\sum_u a_u(x_u-j_u)\geq0\}\)
is a closed halfspace through \(j\). Every point outside the final face has score at most \(-M+\sum_u a_u=-1\), and the intersection on the face is exactly the reduced closed cap. When there are no face operations, use the reduced normal directly. When the reduced tree is empty, use \(\ell(x)\geq\ell(j)\). In all cases the normal is rational and nonzero and \(|H_j\cap A_{m,4}|\leq3^K\). The construction uses coordinate faces and explicit coefficients, with no apex enumeration or numerical optimization.

It remains to translate this certificate to the actual law. Accepted fact 032423921efad6c8 supplies completeness of \(A_{m,4}\) and its exact level census, giving \(\beta_m=\sum_{k=0}^4\eta_m^k\in[1,5]\). Since every actual counting depth is at most \(3^K\),
\[
\Theta_m
=\frac{2^{3n}}{|A_{m,4}|^4}\sum_j\operatorname{dc}_m(j)^3
\leq\frac{3^{3K}}{\beta_m^3},
\qquad
\Psi_m\leq\beta_m3^{3K}\leq5\,3^{3K}.
\]
Accepted fact 01a4100542206b94, applied to this complete support and its actual uniform law with moment exponent three, gives \(\Theta_m\geq1/4\). No probability law has been conditioned or replaced in these conclusions. The upper bound is independent of \(m\), so for this precise family it contradicts both unbounded growth and any eventual bound \(\Theta_m\geq c(\log m)^4\) with fixed \(c>0\). It establishes no assertion about different chain partitions or the differently weighted height construction.
statement:
For every even integer \(m\geq2\), use precisely the construction \(A_{m,4}\subseteq\mathbb Z^{n_{m,4}}\) of accepted fact 032423921efad6c8, choosing its symmetric saturated chain partition by the induction in that fact's proof, with coordinates adjoined in the order \(1,\ldots,m\). No other change is made to its support, successor, or path rule. Write \(n=n_{m,4}=\sum_{s=1}^4m^s\), and let \(u_m\) be the actual uniform probability law on \(A_{m,4}\).

The depth and moment are exactly those of accepted fact 01a4100542206b94, with its \(N=n\), its support \(D=A_{m,4}\), and its probability law \(p=u_m\). In particular, for every \(j\in A_{m,4}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_{u_m}(j)
&=\inf_{\substack{H\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ a closed halfspace}\\j\in H}}u_m(H),
& M_3(u_m)&=\frac1{|A_{m,4}|}\sum_{j\in A_{m,4}}\tau_{u_m}(j)^3,\\
\operatorname{dc}_m(j)
&=|A_{m,4}|\tau_{u_m}(j)
=\min_{\substack{H\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ a closed halfspace}\\j\in H}}|A_{m,4}\cap H|.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(\operatorname{dc}_m\) is only the unnormalized actual counting depth, not the depth of a conditional law on a face. Define \(\beta_m=|A_{m,4}|/2^n\), \(\Theta_m=8^nM_3(u_m)\), and \(\Psi_m=2^{-n}\sum_j\operatorname{dc}_m(j)^3\). These normalization aliases obey \(\Psi_m=\beta_m^4\Theta_m\).

Put \(K=\binom{85}{4}-1\). Then, for every such \(m\) and every \(j\in A_{m,4}\), there is a proper closed halfspace through \(j\), with a rational normal, whose intersection with \(A_{m,4}\) has at most \(3^K\) points. Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{dc}_m(j)&\leq3^K,
&1\leq\beta_m&=\sum_{k=0}^4\eta_m^k\leq5,\\
\frac14\leq\Theta_m&\leq\frac{3^{3K}}{\beta_m^3}\leq3^{3K},
&\Psi_m&\leq5\,3^{3K}.
\end{aligned}
\]
All caps are closed and all boundary points are counted. The locked mixed-integer objects \(C\) and \(S\) are not redefined or changed. This is a theorem about one explicitly specified permissible realization of the exact support; uniform boundedness for an independently chosen different sequence of chain partitions is not claimed.
